primaryResult.interpretation: The opportunity-first Primary contract worked on the first V1.4 window. Both acceptable expressions were positive, benchmark-relative winners and beat the frozen peer control at the pre-registered 60d horizon.

frozenBlockers: mixed expectation path because post-2019 hardware duration was weak
researchDiagnostics.interpretation: The long-duration caution was valid, but the base-horizon order-to-earnings bridge was already realized/explicit and produced large 60d excess. A finite structural half-life does not necessarily imply poor 20-60d opportunity quality when realization occurs well before expiry.

frozenBlockers: high absorption/late-cycle risk after supply-shock rerating
high duration risk because near-term inventories conflicted with later supply exit
researchDiagnostics.interpretation: V1.4 correctly separated near-term inventory uncertainty from the medium-term mine-supply exit, but the promotion gate still over-weighted duration/absorption relative to an already-specified supply catalyst inside the base horizon.

frozenBlockers: mixed path because eventual supply restoration was expected
researchDiagnostics.interpretation: The stock still produced positive base-horizon excess and beat both frozen controls. Long-run normalization risk was real, but it should be separated from whether a strong realized margin engine remains investable over the pre-registered base horizon.

evidence: Generic DRAM was explicitly split into PC stabilization and mobile weakness rather than averaged into one memory call.
Nickel export-ban evidence was split into ex-Indonesia scarcity and Indonesia-processing hypotheses rather than treating opposite economic exposures as one basket.
Selected opportunities were required to be well-scoped before selection.
hypothesisDecomposition.interpretation: The V1.4 decomposition contract behaved as intended and prevented broad-theme substitution.

evidenceHorizonMatrix.interpretation: The matrix successfully preserved near/base/structural disagreement, but existing V1.3 promotion gates still let adverse structural duration veto opportunities whose earnings realization window was materially shorter than the structural expiry.

leaderDivergence.interpretation: The main selected 2019Q3 cases did not require a sector-negative/leader-positive override, so this component remains unproven rather than disproven.

highAbsorptionContinuation.interpretation: The test distinguished fresh earnings/order/supply evidence from narrative repetition, but V1.4 intentionally did not let it override existing High-priority gates.

failureClassDiagnosis.description: The current gates partly answer 'is this a durable multi-quarter structural compounder?' even when the memo's explicit decision validity/base horizon is 60 trading days and the earnings catalyst can realize before a known finite-cycle expiry.
secondary: high absorption is still treated too close to a veto even when new incremental operating evidence is arriving
finite-cycle normalization risk is not explicitly separated from base-horizon earnings convexity
notSupported: Do not infer that all high-momentum or high-valuation names should be promoted.
Do not infer that event half-life is irrelevant.
Do not infer that 120d continuation should validate a 60d decision.
Do not retroactively promote the frozen 2019Q3 Research selections.

nextVersionDecision.reason: 2019Q3 is the first independent window after V1.4 freeze. It validates the decomposition mechanics and exposes a distinct promotion failure: base-horizon realizable opportunities can be blocked by longer-horizon duration/late-cycle rules even when the earnings bridge, acceptable expression and catalyst are already explicit.
requirementsToExplore: Base-horizon catalyst/earnings conversion must be realized or quantitatively bridged and occur materially before the known structural expiry/normalization window.
Acceptable expression must pass balance-sheet/survival, direct exposure and downside checks.
The thesis must have an explicit near/base-horizon expectation gap; long-run normalization may be adverse but cannot be hidden.
High absorption requires fresh incremental information after the prior rerating, not confirmation-only narrative.
A hard re-underwriting/expiry rule must prevent carrying the short-horizon thesis beyond its frozen validity.
This route must not weaken the normal route for long-duration compounders.
nextVersionDecision.validationPolicy: Build V1.5 from this failure class, then freeze it before testing on a different untouched historical window. 2019Q3 cannot validate V1.5.

noSelectionPolicy.interpretation: Nickel and DRAM no-selection children were created specifically because direct product/geography expressions were missing or not base-horizon realized. Do not label these misses by substituting generic theme stocks after reveal; any outcome audit must preserve the frozen child-hypothesis mapping.

prohibitedUses: Do not present this contaminated historical replay as clean alpha validation.
Do not tune V1.4 in place after reveal.
Do not use the spectacular 300552.SZ result to create a named-stock or sector-specific exception.
Do not replace product/geography-specific no-selection hypotheses with hindsight theme proxies.
